spans.claim: Hugh Curran died of hydrocyanic acid poisoning
spans.anchor: this man died of poison,--Hydrocyanic acid
spans.span: yes, this man died of poison,--Hydrocyanic acid.

spans.claim: The room was locked from the inside with no forced entry
spans.anchor: the room was locked and there’s no bottle or paper to be found

spans.claim: Poison was administered via a toothpick
spans.anchor: the instrument of death, for I could find no other
spans.span: At any rate I did conclude that the instrument of death, for I could find no other.

spans.claim: Angel Bob Baldwin gave Curran the toothpick
spans.anchor: Mr. Baldwin had given Curran that Club toothpick
spans.span: Of course, I knew that Mr. Baldwin had given Curran that Club toothpick, and it seemed a clever deduction.

spans.claim: The poisoned toothpick was replaced with a clean one
spans.anchor: he adroitly substituted a clean one for the other
spans.span: Baldwin is the clever criminal, he is the ingenious book thief,--it was he who provided the poisoned toothpick, and after it had done its work, he adroitly substituted a clean one for the other and placed it in Curran's waste-basket.

spans.claim: Pauline Fuller is the divorced wife of Hugh Curran
spans.anchor: Miss Fuller is the divorced wife of Hugh Curran

spans.claim: Pauline took Curran’s watch and hid it in her desk
spans.anchor: I found Hugh Curran’s watch hidden in a locked desk

spans.claim: Pauline fled the house after the murder
spans.anchor: Pauline Fuller has disappeared

spans.claim: Ned Knox was jealous but innocent
spans.anchor: Ned Knox was the one who advocated shooting

spans.claim: Anna Knox was seen on the balcony with Curran
spans.anchor: Mrs. Knox,--I know her well. She had on a bee-yooutiful gown
spans.span: yes, sir, it was Mrs. Knox,--I know her well. She had on a bee-yooutiful gown,--dressing-gown,--what they call negglegy, you know.

spans.claim: The missing catalogue page was from 'Gammer Gurton’s Needle'
spans.anchor: the catalogue that contained ‘The Needle’

spans.claim: Baldwin bought the missing page at auction
spans.anchor: the page went to the other bidder
spans.span: At last the agent kept on against one other only, and finally as two hundred was overbid, Fibsy's agent ceased, and the page went to the other bidder.

spans.claim: Baldwin committed suicide after exposure
spans.anchor: he popped something into his mouth and swallowed it

spans.claim: Fleming Stone discovered the puncture wound in Curran’s jaw
spans.anchor: a small puncture in the jaw of the dead man
spans.span: That is a small puncture in the jaw of the dead man, through which, there can be no doubt, the poison was introduced into his system.

spans.claim: The poison was hydrocyanic acid applied via toothpick
spans.anchor: poisoned toothpick dipped in hydrocyanic acid

spans.claim: The door was locked from inside by the victim
spans.anchor: Mr. Curran let him out

spans.claim: Pauline Fuller visited Curran’s room to retrieve her picture
spans.anchor: I went to his room at two o’clock

spans.claim: Pauline Fuller did not kill Curran
spans.anchor: No, I didn’t kill him,--though I confess there was murder in my heart
spans.span: No, I didn't kill him,--though I confess there was murder in my heart.

spans.claim: Fibsy McGuire used radio broadcasts to locate Pauline
spans.anchor: I got a chap I know to write a song about the ‘Valentine a waitin’ for Pauline’

spans.claim: Valentine Loft forgives Pauline and marries her
spans.anchor: We’re going to be married in a few minutes
spans.span: We're going to be married in a few minutes," Loft replied, kissing her in the exuberance of his happiness.
